topics.title: Cells and Microscopy
topics.objective: Apply knowledge of cell structure, specialised cells and magnification calculations with the light microscope.

topics.title: Biological Molecules and Enzymes
topics.objective: Apply knowledge of food tests, biological molecules and enzyme action, specificity and denaturation.

topics.title: Nutrition and Digestion
topics.objective: Apply knowledge of photosynthesis, leaf structure, the human digestive system and a balanced diet.

topics.title: Movement into and out of Cells
topics.objective: Apply knowledge of diffusion, osmosis and active transport across partially permeable membranes.

topics.title: Respiration and Gas Exchange
topics.objective: Apply knowledge of aerobic and anaerobic respiration, the breathing system and alveolar gas exchange.

topics.title: Reproduction and Development
topics.objective: Apply knowledge of mitosis and meiosis, flower structure, pollination, fertilisation and human development.

topics.title: Genetics and Inheritance
topics.objective: Apply knowledge of genes and chromosomes, monohybrid crosses, mutation and patterns of variation.

topics.title: Ecology and Ecosystems
topics.objective: Apply knowledge of food chains, energy flow, the carbon and nitrogen cycles and human impacts on ecosystems.

questions.prompt: Which cell structure is present in a plant cell but absent from an animal cell?

The cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria are found in both cell types, so none of them can distinguish a plant cell from an animal cell.

questions.workedSolution: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole in addition to the structures they share with animal cells. The cell membrane, cytoplasm and mitochondria are found in both cell types, so none of them can distinguish a plant cell from an animal cell. Therefore the correct answer is A: Cell wall.

options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Magnification = image size ÷ actual size = 45 mm ÷ 0.15 mm = 300, so the drawing is ×300 the size of the real cell. ×30 comes from a slip in the division, ×6.75 results from multiplying instead of dividing (45 × 0.15), and ×3000 comes from misplacing the decimal point.

questions.prompt: A microscope has an eyepiece lens of ×10 and objective lenses of ×4, ×10 and ×40. Which combination gives a total magnification of ×400?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Total magnification = eyepiece magnification × objective magnification = 10 × 40 = 400. The ×4 objective gives only ×40 and the ×10 objective gives ×100, and a light microscope image is always viewed through the eyepiece, so the objective cannot be used alone.

options.label: D
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: Total magnification = eyepiece magnification × objective magnification = 10 × 40 = 400. The ×4 objective gives only ×40 and the ×10 objective gives ×100, and a light microscope image is always viewed through the eyepiece, so the objective cannot be used alone. Therefore the correct answer is C: Eyepiece ×10 with objective ×40.

options.text: The mirror, to admit more light
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.text: The eyepiece, changing it for a higher-power lens
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. At high power only the fine adjustment knob should be used to focus, because the objective lens is very close to the slide and the coarse knob could drive the lens into the slide. The mirror or lamp changes brightness rather than sharpness, and swapping the eyepiece changes magnification without focusing the image.

questions.prompt: Root hair cells absorb water from the soil efficiently. Which feature of a root hair cell increases the surface area available for absorption?

options.label: A
options.text: A long hair-like projection extending into the soil
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. The root hair is a slender extension of the cell that greatly increases the surface area to volume ratio for the absorption of water and mineral ions. Root hair cells grow underground so they contain no chloroplasts, their cell wall stays thin to let water pass, and the vacuole holds cell sap rather than starch grains.

options.label: B

options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D

questions.prompt: Which row correctly matches a specialised animal cell with its adaptation?

options.label: A
options.text: Red blood cell — has a large nucleus to store more DNA

options.label: B

Therefore the correct answer is B: Ciliated cell — has cilia that beat to move mucus along the airways.

questions.prompt: A food sample is heated with Benedict's solution and the mixture changes from blue to brick-red. What does this result show?

options.label: A
options.text: A reducing sugar is present in the sample
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. When heated, reducing sugars such as glucose and maltose reduce the blue copper(II) ions in Benedict's solution to a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide. Starch is a non-reducing sugar and gives no colour change with Benedict's, protein is detected by the Biuret test, and the brick-red colour itself proves that a sugar is present.

options.label: B
options.text: Starch is present in the sample
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: Protein is present in the sample
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: The sample contains no sugar of any kind
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: When heated, reducing sugars such as glucose and maltose reduce the blue copper(II) ions in Benedict's solution to a brick-red precipitate of copper(I) oxide. Starch is a non-reducing sugar and gives no colour change with Benedict's, protein is detected by the Biuret test, and the brick-red colour itself proves that a sugar is present. Therefore the correct answer is A: A reducing sugar is present in the sample.

questions.prompt: Amylase in human saliva works best at about 37 °C. Why does the enzyme stop working when it is boiled?

options.label: A
options.text: The enzyme molecules are used up by the reaction
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: The high temperature changes the shape of the active site so the substrate no longer fits
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Boiling denatures the enzyme: the bonds holding the protein in its shape break, the active site changes shape and the substrate can no longer bind to it. Enzymes are catalysts and are not used up by the reaction, boiling the enzyme does not alter the starch substrate, and enzymes are denatured rather than accelerated at 100 °C.

options.label: C
options.text: Boiling changes the substrate into a different molecule
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: The enzyme works fastest at 100 °C so the reaction runs out of substrate
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

questions.workedSolution: Boiling denatures the enzyme: the bonds holding the protein in its shape break, the active site changes shape and the substrate can no longer bind to it. Enzymes are catalysts and are not used up by the reaction, boiling the enzyme does not alter the starch substrate, and enzymes are denatured rather than accelerated at 100 °C. Therefore the correct answer is B: The high temperature changes the shape of the active site so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.prompt: Which enzyme digests protein in the stomach?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why an enzyme catalyses only one reaction?

options.label: A
options.text: Enzymes are destroyed after catalysing one reaction
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: B
options.text: Each enzyme works equally well at any temperature and pH
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: All substrate molecules have exactly the same shape
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: D
options.text: The shape of the active site is complementary to only one substrate molecule
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Each enzyme's active site has a shape that fits only its own substrate, like a lock and key, so the enzyme catalyses only one reaction. Enzymes remain unchanged after the reaction, each enzyme has its own narrow optimum temperature and pH, and substrates differ in shape, which is exactly why specificity arises.

questions.workedSolution: Each enzyme's active site has a shape that fits only its own substrate, like a lock and key, so the enzyme catalyses only one reaction. Enzymes remain unchanged after the reaction, each enzyme has its own narrow optimum temperature and pH, and substrates differ in shape, which is exactly why specificity arises. Therefore the correct answer is D: The shape of the active site is complementary to only one substrate molecule.

questions.prompt: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of…

options.label: B
options.text: high temperature to a region of low temperature
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

options.label: C
options.text: higher concentration to a region of lower concentration
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Diffusion is the net movement of particles down their concentration gradient, from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, as a result of their random motion. Movement from low to high concentration is active transport, and temperature or pressure differences are not part of the definition of diffusion.

options.label: D
options.text: high pressure to a region of low pressure
options.rationale: This option is a plausible misconception, but it conflicts with the principle established in the worked solution.

Therefore the correct answer is C: higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
